extracted.intended_audience: researchers, data scientists, and policymakers constructing or using regulatory measurement datasets (RegData users; regulatory economists)
extracted.subtask_description: Creating a national RegData panel by applying machine‑learning text analysis to Australian acts and legislative instruments to quantify regulatory restrictiveness and enable comparative/regression analysis. Includes corpus collection, cleaning, keyword selection, industry classification, and analytic normalizations (per capita, log transformations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory restrictions metric (restrictive clauses)
rubrics_metrics.description: Counts the number of keywords likely to impose binding constraints on citizens or businesses — RDAU1.0 uses five such words: 'shall,' 'must,' 'may not,' 'prohibited,' and 'required.' These are the 'regulatory restrictions' that measure the extent to which a regulation prohibits or requires certain acts or behaviors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outputs are 'restriction counts' within a given document of the federal corpus; considered the closest measure to real regulatory effect (more accurate than word or page counts).

rubrics_metrics.name: Word count as a proxy for regulatory content
rubrics_metrics.description: Word count is closer to a measure of legislative and regulatory content than page counts but includes explanatory content, preambles, appendices, and other extraneous material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Word counts validate and complement restrictive clause counts but are less accurate because they don't distinguish between restrictive and explanatory language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Page count / file size measures (baseline)
rubrics_metrics.description: Measuring regulation by number of regulations, page counts, or file size provides a crude quantification but maps imperfectly to economic consequences because of layout/font/format differences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page/file size measures are the least accurate and should be treated as supportive rather than primary evidence of restrictiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection of keyword suite (carefully selected verbs and adjectives)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a carefully selected suite of verbs/adjectives to identify restrictions (RegData examples: 'shall', 'must', 'may not', 'prohibited', 'required').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keywords should capture binding constraints; selection determines what is counted as a restriction and therefore affects measurement validity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industry decomposition via industry-specific training documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify relevance of regulatory text to industries using industry-specific training documents (intended for two- through six-digit industry codes; for Australia, ANZSIC codes are appropriate).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accurate industry attribution requires locally relevant training docs (ANZSIC-based); using NAICS training materials for Australia yields results of unknown accuracy and should be replaced by Australian training documents for reliable decomposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attribution of regulations to acts (vs agencies)
rubrics_metrics.description: In Australia, attribute regulations to particular acts rather than to agencies because Australian regulations originate in parliamentary acts and ministerial instruments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat the act and its legislative instruments as one regulatory regime when decomposing origin-of-regulation; this differs from the US approach that attributes to agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manual corpus collection from ComLaw with reaggregation
rubrics_metrics.description: Collect the corpus by downloading acts and legislative instruments from the ComLaw repository and reaggregate multipart volumes into single analytical units (e.g., Corporations Act 2001 — five volumes → one document).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manual download was required because no CFR-like centralized annual compilation exists; reaggregation avoids under- or double-counting caused by split volumes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize start and end dates to avoid double-counting
rubrics_metrics.description: Enable RDAU1.0 to recognize start and end dates of acts and regulations to avoid double- or triple-counting content when successive acts update/replace earlier acts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many historical acts lack listed end dates in ComLaw; without date recognition the system may treat obsolete and superseded acts as concurrently current, inflating restriction counts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclude repealed/cancelled/expired documents (red-flag filtering)
rubrics_metrics.description: Examine document index labels for red-flag words like 'repealed,' 'cancelled,' or 'expired' and filter such documents out of a corpus intended to represent current law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These documents often have very low word counts (only a sentence or two) and should be removed during download or cleaning to avoid contaminating time-series measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum word count quality check
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine the minimum word count of the corpus and count how many documents are at that level; many low-word-count documents indicate compromised text quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Low word counts often result from difficulties converting originals into digitized text (OCR or scraping errors); flag and remediate conversion issues before analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duplicate detection and resolution in metadata
rubrics_metrics.description: Check the metadata file for duplicates, which may indicate insufficiently specific indexing, mixed versions, or human processing errors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigate duplicate causes (appendices, mixed versions, out-of-date text not deleted) and clean metadata to ensure each analytical unit is unique and correctly versioned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure numeric index elements are numeric
rubrics_metrics.description: If corpus index elements are intended to be numeric (integers/floats), coerce or clean values to numeric types to detect unwanted characters or text in numeric fields.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programmatic enforcement of numeric types reveals indexing errors; fix by reorganizing/cleaning index values for consistent numeric treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handle historical coverage and digitization limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that older acts/regulations (pre-1970s/early years) may be missing from the online repository because they were not digitized, limiting historical coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be cautious interpreting long-run series; treat data before reliable digitization (authors: late 1990s / 1997 onward) as lower quality and document gaps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations: exclude state/territory legislation in federal panel
rubrics_metrics.description: RDAU1.0 covers federal (Commonwealth) acts and instruments only and does not include state and territory legislation, which causes underestimation of total national regulatory volume.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledge scope limitation; future extensions should add subnational corpora for comprehensive national measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manual sifting for obsolete or obviously incorrect documents
rubrics_metrics.description: After initial download, manually sift and remove obviously obsolete or erroneous documents that were stored on the official site.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manual review is required to remove obsolete documents and to correct repository artifacts not handled by automated collection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reaggregate multipart acts/volumes into single analytical units
rubrics_metrics.description: Some large acts are split into multiple volumes which should be reaggregated to avoid undercounting or treating volumes as separate acts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify multi-volume acts (e.g., Corporations Act 2001) and combine volumes into a single document for consistent treatment in counts and time-series.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion of guidance documents and soft law
rubrics_metrics.description: RegData explicitly does not include guidance documents, memos of interpretation, or other forms of 'soft law'; it covers only actual regulations (administrative law) in the corpus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Researchers should note this limitation: de facto regulation via guidance is not captured and may require separate effort to quantify.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidence window / trusted years (digitization-based)
rubrics_metrics.description: Because digitization is uneven, treat RegData estimates as most reliable from the late 1990s/1997 onward when regulatory data were reliably digitized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When comparing jurisdictions or time-series, truncate or weight analyses to years with reliable digital records to avoid artifacts from missing historical data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Words per restrictive clause (wordiness metric)
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute words per restrictive clause to capture changes in legislative wordiness (authors observe words per restriction roughly doubled since 1975 and shifted in the 1990s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this metric to analyze shifts in drafting style, bureaucratic expansion, or explanatory vs. restrictive content; interpret increases with caution and consider multiple hypotheses (supply-side, demand-side, bureaucratic incentives).

rubrics_metrics.name: Normalization and comparative analytic choices (per capita & log transformations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Normalize restriction counts by population (per capita) and consider log-log transformations for regression analysis when testing scaling hypotheses (e.g., Mulligan and Shleifer's fixed-cost population hypothesis).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Per capita and logged analyses help test scaling relationships; authors use both level-level and log-log regressions and report correlations and elasticity estimates (e.g., 10% population → ~1.87% restrictions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scalable granularity of search results & search-term weightings
rubrics_metrics.description: RegData supports scalable granularity for search results (title-level to paragraph-level) and uses search-term weightings (e.g., derived from Google Ngram in earlier RegData versions) to refine counts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjust granularity and term weightings to match the corpus structure and analytic goals; document the chosen granularity for reproducibility.
